status_summary: No proposal to split CDC into separate data-publishing and public health policy agencies was found as of 2026-10-08. HHS announced a different restructuring on 2025-03-27: about 10,000 job cuts department-wide, a proposed Administration for a Healthy America (AHA) combining several agencies, and the preparedness office (ASPR) moving into CDC; CDC's chief operating officer put the net CDC staff reduction at 24 percent by June 2025. Nineteen states and the District of Columbia challenged the restructuring in New York v. Kennedy (D.R.I., Judge DuBose), and on 2025-07-01 the court granted a preliminary injunction, finding the states likely to succeed on claims that HHS acted arbitrarily and capriciously and contrary to law in disrupting congressionally mandated functions; the First Circuit denied the government's emergency stay request on 2025-09-17, the government voluntarily dismissed its appeal about six weeks later, and on 2026-04-07 the court denied a motion to dismiss the amended complaint. Congress did not create AHA in the fiscal year 2026 Labor-HHS appropriation (Division B of Public Law 119-75, approved 2026-02-03; House passage 2026-01-22), and trade-group reporting on the conference agreement says it rejected major restructuring at CDC. The fiscal year 2027 request (Budget in Brief released 2026-04-03) repeats the approach: CDC budget authority of $5.280 billion versus $5.764 billion for fiscal year 2026 (a $484 million reduction), a new National Center for Chemicals and Toxins inside CDC, several CDC programs moved to AHA, and a cross-reference in the CDC chapter to the Office of Strategy chapter for the National Center for Health Statistics. A statistical-community post of 2026-04-03 quoting HHS's justification reports that the request proposes moving the National Center for Health Statistics from CDC to a to-be-created Office of Strategy, continuing a planned reorganization, with $175 million proposed for the center; that is the only element found that points toward separating a data function from CDC, and it is a budget proposal that does not create an agency with a legal duty to publish state-sourced data. Erica Schwartz was confirmed as CDC director on 2026-08-05.

timeline.event: HHS announces a department restructuring: roughly 10,000 full-time positions cut, 28 divisions consolidated to 15, a new Administration for a Healthy America (combining the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health, HRSA, SAMHSA, ATSDR and NIOSH), and ASPR moved to CDC.
Government Executive reports CDC has shed about one quarter of its staff, net of about 800 reduction-in-force notices rescinded from roughly 2,400 issued in April 2025.

In New York v. Kennedy (D.R.I. No. 25-cv-196; 19 states and the District of Columbia) the court grants a preliminary injunction against parts of HHS's 2025-03-27 restructuring, finding the states likely to succeed on claims that HHS acted arbitrarily and capriciously and contrary to law, and that the announcement and resulting reduction-in-force notices were reviewable final agency action; the components at issue include CDC laboratory services, the Division of Reproductive Health, NIOSH, the National Center for Environmental Health and HIV, STD and TB prevention. The court makes no separate finding about AHA. Bloomberg Law reported on 2025-07-18 that the court declined to lift the injunction and denied a stay pending appeal.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island (via govinfo)

timeline.event: House passes the final FY2026 Labor-HHS agreement; reporting says it does not establish the Administration for a Healthy America and rejects major restructuring at CDC, HRSA, NIH and SAMHSA.

The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75, H.R. 7148) is approved on 2026-02-03; Division B is the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education appropriations act. The text of Division B could not be read; the statements that it does not establish AHA or fund major CDC restructuring rest on the trade-group report of 2026-01-22.

HHS's fiscal year 2027 Budget in Brief (release date per a law firm alert) proposes CDC budget authority of $5.280 billion (down $484 million from $5.764 billion), a National Center for Chemicals and Toxins in CDC, and moving CDC injury prevention, birth defects, chronic disease and HIV programs to the Administration for a Healthy America; the CDC chapter refers readers to the Office of Strategy chapter for the National Center for Health Statistics. The statistical community's post of the same date (American Statistical Association) quotes HHS's justification as proposing to move the National Center for Health Statistics from CDC to the to-be-created Office of Strategy, with $175.3 million proposed; the Office of Strategy chapter itself could not be read.

The Rhode Island court (No. 25-cv-196) denies the government's motion to dismiss the amended complaint; all five counts (separation of powers, Appropriations Clause, ultra vires, and two APA counts) proceed. The order notes the First Circuit denied the government's emergency stay request on 2025-09-17 and that the government voluntarily dismissed its appeal of the preliminary injunction about six weeks later; it does not specifically address CDC.

timeline.event: Senate confirms Erica Schwartz as CDC director (51 to 44), ending a vacancy that began when the prior director was removed in August 2025.

title: Split CDC into a data-publishing agency and a separate public health policy agency
uncertainties: The finding that no CDC split was proposed rests on HHS announcements, the fiscal year 2027 Budget in Brief (the readable text of the PDF ends at about page 39, before the Office of Strategy chapter), the KFF HHS tracker (updated 2026-08-19) and press searches; congress.gov bill text was not searched, so a bill introduced by members of Congress cannot be excluded. The proposed move of the National Center for Health Statistics to the Office of Strategy is reported by an American Statistical Association post quoting HHS's justification; the HHS document was not found, so this rests on a secondary source. If the proposal is confirmed in the HHS document, a later review could consider whether proposed with a partial or parallel match fits better than diverged, because it separates a data function from CDC without creating the publishing agency the Mandate describes. The fiscal year 2026 signing date (2026-02-03) is now backed by govinfo's header for Public Law 119-75, whose Division B is the Labor-HHS act, but Division B's text could not be read, and the statement that the agreement rejected major CDC restructuring comes from a trade-group newsletter. The court orders were read through fetch summaries; the 2025-07-01 order's operative paragraphs were cut off, so the exact scope of the injunction was not confirmed. The dismissal of the government's appeal is dated only as about six weeks after 2025-09-17, per the 2026-04-07 order. The KFF tracker lists a 2025-07-08 Supreme Court action allowing federal job cuts to proceed; how it bears on the Rhode Island injunction was not verified, and this record does not rely on it. The label diverged with match partial is a judgment call: the administration restructured CDC along different lines rather than splitting data from policy.
